summary_hint: Tells a processor which property, who inspected, when, and whether the property is clear.

nested_lists.name: findings

fields.name: category
fields.why: processor — live insect / dead-or-evidence / visible damage

fields.name: insect_or_damage_type
fields.why: processor — the insect or damage type of the finding

fields.name: location
fields.why: processor — where the finding was observed

rejected.reason: folded into the flattened inspection-company fields

rejected.name: effective_date, expiration_date, statement_period_start/_end, document_issue_date

rejected.reason: seller/buyer names rarely drive a decision here; leave to catch-all

rejected.reason: inspector signature folded into inspector_name; not notarized/versioned

rejected.name: live_insects_findings, dead_insects_or_evidence_findings, visible_damage_findings
rejected.reason: consolidated into the single findings list

rejected.name: recommended_actions_or_treatments
rejected.reason: folded into findings (or catch-all); a second list is not justified by any rule

rejected.name: seller_or_owner_disclosure_signature, buyer_acknowledgment_signature
rejected.reason: acknowledgment signatures; no rule, low processor value

encoding_variations: Clearance is stated three ways: an explicit 'no visible evidence' checkbox (no_visible_evidence_indicator), a 'no action recommended' checkbox (no_action_recommended_indicator), or prose in the findings section — the two flags plus the findings list together disambiguate, since a report can find evidence yet recommend no action (old, treated damage)
Form section letters differ (NPMA-33 uses graphic diagrams and Section II/III; state forms use 'Section 1/Section 2') — form_version is the disambiguator
Insect types abbreviated ('SUBT' subterranean termite, 'DW' drywood, 'PPB' powderpost beetle) — capture verbatim

open_questions.q: Consolidating three finding lists into one.
options: a single findings flat-row list with a category column (live insect / dead-or-evidence / visible damage)
preserving the catalog's three separate object[] fields
open_questions.recommendation: a single findings flat-row list with a category column; confirm this is acceptable vs preserving the catalog's three separate object[] fields

open_questions.q: obstructions_and_inaccessible_areas (CORE object[]) not nested. It genuinely repeats and is CORE (limits of inspection completeness), but a second nested list exceeds the one-list budget with no rule demanding it.
open_questions.recommendation: flatten to a joined str unless a completeness rule is planned

open_questions.q: Boolean flags degraded to str. no_visible_evidence_indicator / no_action_recommended_indicator have no bool coercer.
open_questions.recommendation: confirm downstream reads them as strings, not typed booleans

notes: This is the inspection (findings) document, distinct from the completion/clearance certificate (packet 096).
The two boolean-ish flags can disagree with the findings prose (evidence of prior, treated activity with no current action) — capture all three; do not force consistency.
Capture the inspector's license and the business license as distinct numbers.
No PII requiring registration — business/inspector license numbers are professional identifiers, not personal PII; no SSN/DOB/account fields appear on a termite report.
